approach.why: The fix (e460de70a655, merged at 3d5933f31b83) changes the two probes at the layer the held findings named rather than special-casing the reproductions. Erasure: parse_schema returns a Schema whose FKs carry a name (explicit CONSTRAINT or Postgres default <table>_<cols>_fkey via pg_default_name with NAMEDATALEN truncation); DROP/RENAME CONSTRAINT, DROP [COLUMN] and DROP TABLE remove or rename them; Probe B compares the raw REFERENCES feedback count against every FK ever declared (declared_to_feedback) so a drop cannot unbalance it; an unresolvable dropped/renamed name that is not a default _pkey/_key/_check/_excl fails closed (oracle.py:509-535, 561-597, 722-738). Host binding: Probe E scans every .nest/.nest_service in the api crate, fails closed on a non-literal prefix, flags any literal prefix that is a whole-segment prefix of a ROUTE_HOMES path outside that path's home fn, and compares path parameters by position via _segments (oracle.py:643-706, 724-726). Verified on a scratch copy through the in-tree runners: mutations.py for all three oracles exits 0 (clean copy green; E5-E8, F1-F4, G1, G2 red; H1-H6 red; M12 red). G1 is the held C-001 reproduction verbatim and H5 the held C-002 reproduction verbatim; both now exit 1. Both oracles exit 0 on the real tree, and the real migrations' existing DROP CONSTRAINTs (feedback_body_check, submit_idempotency_pkey, feedback_short_code_key) resolve as non-FK defaults, so nothing in the tree trips the fail-closed branch. Beyond the recorded rows, on a scratch copy via --spec: a drop-and-re-add of the CASCADE FK (two statements, or one ALTER with DROP CONSTRAINT, ADD CONSTRAINT) stays green, so the common migration pattern is not a false positive; rename-then-drop, drop-then-re-add as SET NULL, and DROP COLUMN feedback_id go red; a .nest at the board prefix inside board_router stays green, while a const prefix, a {pid} prefix and a .nest_service("/api", ..) in health_router go red. The window's own commit 84ea85388894 changes two README lines (finding ids). The whole suite exited 0 in the checkout at 3b9cadbc (finalize-gates.jsonl 2026-10-13T20:26:48Z, head 3b9cadbc, tree d839c192, `bash scripts/ci-local.sh --tests --frontends exit 0`). Nothing the fix touches is broken.

So the backstop measures the 13 oracle lanes and cargo clippy only, and the prompt's 'whole suite: pass' rests on the checkout run at finalize-gates.jsonl ran_at 2026-10-13T20:26:48Z (exit 0), not on the backstop (VER-40/42). Outside this window's diff: the fix is in the backstop runner (lib/uldf/backstop.py: npm ci in the copy, or run against a tree with node_modules; pass DATABASE_URL into its env) and belongs in the framework source at S:/ULDF/claude-template, or as a hazard entry. Low because no check claimed a pass it did not earn; the cost is a backstop that cannot catch a post-push regression in cargo test or the front ends.

findings.summary: The closing session verified by repetition and polling where parking would do: tsc -b run 4x with no edit between, two reruns after a failure with no edit, and a background verification polled 14 times over 25.7 min
findings.evidence: verification-demand lines in the prompt, session 8c0335d2 (the closing session; request.json session = 8c0335d2-b0cf-486b-9f49-21b7e0f44fc0): `static: npx tsc -b` run 4 times with no code edit between (0.9 min); `unit: cargo test -p feedbackmonk-api --test board_admin --test board_admin_privacy` rerun 1 time after a failure with no edit (4.5 min); `unit: npx vitest run` rerun 1 time after a failure with no edit (1.4 min); polled a background verification 14 times (25.7 min), 5 times (5.7 min), 3 times (1.9 min). None of these touched the window's diff (two README lines). The program that owns the wait is the background check with the session parked on it (CLAUDE.md 'Wait by parking, never by polling'); a rerun after a failure with no edit re-grades a tree a check already graded. Not a defect in the tree; recorded so the next window can see whether the habit persists.
